# AWS CodeCommit

Manage CodeCommit repositories, tags and CloudFormation resources, and host their content as real git repositories over smart HTTP.

**Status: implemented subset.** Operation selection does not imply complete input or behavior parity.

| Contract | Current implementation |
| --- | --- |
| Service ID | `codecommit` |
| Signing name | `codecommit` |
| Wire protocol | AWS JSON 1.1 |
| API version | `2015-04-13` |
| Scope | Account and region |
| Execution | Records, with real git repositories served over smart HTTP (requires git) |
| Selected operations | 20 of 80 in the pinned model |

## Implemented behavior

See the [implemented feature catalogue](catalogue.md#aws-codecommit) for this service's capabilities.

Repository content is real git: see [CodeCommit git hosting](../guides/codecommit-git.md) for the local clone URL, how the account and Region are chosen, credentials, the `git` requirement and the default branch.

## Limitations and future work

- Git content needs the git executable on PATH (the Docker image includes it); without it repository records still work and every content operation fails with ServiceUnavailableException. SSH transport and public key management are not provided.
- No pull requests, comments, approval rules, merges, merge conflict APIs, BatchGetCommits, GetBlob, DeleteFile, ListFileCommitHistory or other operations outside the selected set.
- No repository triggers or webhooks; EventBridge repository state events are published but no notification triggers run.
- PutFile and CreateCommit do not accept sourceFile or keepEmptyFolders; GetDifferences does not compare different beforePath and afterPath; GetFile and GetFolder specifiers are a branch, tag, HEAD, fully qualified reference or commit ID, not git revision expressions.
- TinyStack bounds are not AWS quotas: CodeCommit JSON requests are limited to 64 MiB and ListBranches pages at 1,000 branches; git pushes have no size limit. KMS keys do not encrypt repository content and UpdateRepositoryEncryptionKey is not implemented.
- In parse mode git sends credentials only after a challenge, which TinyStack does not issue, so choose an account or an IAM user with http.extraHeader (or http.proactiveAuth); without credentials the default account is used and, under identity.authorization enforce, the anonymous caller is denied.
- CloudFormation Code (repository seeding from S3) and Triggers properties fail explicitly, and so does a KmsKeyId change.

These gaps describe current boundaries and possible follow-up slices. The [roadmap](../roadmap/index.md)
separates proposed work from registered functionality; there are no promised release dates.
